newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Safeway workers back on job after strike.
newsitem.headline: Canada Safeway workers back on job after strike.

text.p: Unionized employees at 74 Canada Safeway Ltd. grocery stores in the Western Canadian province of Alberta returned to work on Monday, ending a bitter 75-day strike.

Canada Safeway, a unit of Pleasanton, Calif.-based Safeway Inc. -- North America's second largest grocery chain -- said it expected most of its 10,000 clerks, cashiers and meat-cutters to be back on the job after agreeing to a mediated settlement on Sunday.

"We are pleased that our employees will soon be back at work," Canada Safeway President Grant Hansen said in a statement. "The dispute has been difficult for the company, our employees and our customers."
The company and its unions turned to a mediator to help get bargaining restarted after negotiations bogged down in the dispute, which began in late March.

Under the settlement that runs until March 2001, the main union involved, the United Food and Commercial Workers, failed to secure sought-after wage increases for all employees, who took rollbacks in 1993 to help the company avert a financial crisis.
But it secured a guaranteed number of working hours for part-time staff, who make up most of the workforce at Alberta's biggest grocery chain.
Safeway had insisted that its pay structure remain in line with that of its competitors in the province, which include Toronto-based Loblaw Cos. Ltd. and several co-opratives.

Management and replacement workers kept the Safeway stores open during the strike, but about half Safeway's regular customers switched to shopping at competitors' stores, according to independent estimates.
Union officials said they expected more controversy after an estimated 2,000 workers crossed picket lines during the strike.
Unionized Canada Safeway staff had been without a contract since March 1996.
Safeway shares were up 50 cents to $47.750 on Monday on the New York Stock Exchange.
